items.text: Among adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction referred to the new nurse-led titration clinic from November 2026, will at least 60 percent be on at least half the target dose of every indicated medicine class within 6 months of referral, without potassium above 6.0 mmol/L in more than 3 percent?
items.population: Adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction referred to the clinic
items.intervention: Nurse-led titration under the signed-off protocol, fortnightly clinic or telephone visits
items.comparator: Six-month baseline from the clinic list before the clinic opened
items.outcome: Proportion at half target dose or more of all indicated classes at 6 months
items.time: 6 months from referral; first review after 12 months of operation
items.setting: District general hospital heart failure service

finer: Feasible within 6 nurse hours per week and existing data; interesting to the directorate; not novel by design, because the service applies established evidence; ethical as a registered service evaluation; relevant because most patients are under-dosed.
summary: One time-bound service aim with a safety limit.
